bib.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

read.skipped: Figures not viewed as images; plotted values (Figs 3-5, 8, 9, 12, 13) unread beyond captions and text.

question: Can a standard Transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches, with minimal image-specific inductive bias, match or beat CNNs on image classification when pre-trained at large scale?
hypothesis: Large scale training trumps inductive bias: a pure Transformer lacking CNN locality and translation equivariance will underperform on small data but match or exceed ResNets when pre-trained on 14M-300M images.
contributions: Vision Transformer (ViT): split image into fixed-size patches, linearly embed, add position embeddings, feed to a standard Transformer encoder with a [class] token
Show that pre-training on ImageNet-21k or JFT-300M and transferring gives state-of-the-art or near-SOTA results on ImageNet, CIFAR-100, VTAB at lower pre-training compute than BiT or Noisy Student
Controlled studies of pre-training data size, compute scaling, position embeddings, class token vs GAP, and a preliminary masked-patch self-supervision experiment

method.summary: A standard BERT-style Transformer encoder (pre-norm, GELU MLP) takes flattened 16x16 or 14x14 (or 32x32) image patches linearly projected to D dims plus learnable 1D position embeddings and a prepended [class] token. Models are pre-trained supervised on ImageNet, ImageNet-21k or JFT-300M with Adam and fine-tuned with SGD on downstream tasks at higher resolution, compared against BiT ResNets and hybrids.

datasets.name: ObjectNet

models.name: ViT-Base
models.architecture: pre-norm Transformer encoder, GELU MLP, [class] token, learnable 1D position embeddings
models.context: inferred: N=HW/P^2 patches plus [class]; 196 patches at 224 with P=16, 49 with P=32

other.variants: B/16, B/32; adopted directly from BERT
L/16, L/32; adopted directly from BERT

models.name: ResNet (BiT)
models.architecture: ResNet with Group Normalization instead of BatchNorm and standardized convolutions

models.name: Hybrid R50+ViT
models.architecture: ResNet50 feature maps fed to ViT with patch size 1x1; stage-4 output or extended stage 3 (4x longer sequence)

other.naming: number at end is total downsampling ratio of the ResNet backbone, not patch size

other.note: numbers taken from literature (Xie et al. 2020)

training.objective: supervised classification (pre-training head: MLP with one tanh hidden layer; fine-tuning: single zero-initialized linear layer D x K); self-supervised variant: masked patch prediction of 3-bit mean colour (512 classes)
training.optimizer: Adam beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999 for pre-training all models including ResNets; SGD momentum 0.9 for fine-tuning
training.lr: pre-train base LR per Table 3: ViT-B 8e-4, ViT-L/32 6e-4, ViT-L/16 4e-4, ViT-H/14 3e-4 on JFT; 1e-3 on ImageNet-21k; 3e-3 on ImageNet. Fine-tune grid per Table 4 (e.g. ImageNet {0.003,0.01,0.03,0.06}; VTAB 0.01)
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then linear decay for JFT and ImageNet-21k; cosine for ImageNet from scratch; fine-tuning cosine decay
training.steps: fine-tuning: ImageNet 20 000, CIFAR100 10 000, CIFAR10 10 000, Pets 500, Flowers 500, VTAB 2 500; self-supervised: 1M steps
training.epochs: JFT: 7 (B, L/32, L/16 short), 14 (L/16 long, H/14); ImageNet-21k: 90 (B), 30/90 (L); ImageNet: 300
training.seq_len: inferred: 196 patches + [class] at 224 with 16x16 patches; fine-tuning at 384 gives 576+1
training.weight_decay: 0.1 on JFT (and hybrids/ResNets); 0.03 on ImageNet-21k; 0.3 on ImageNet; none in fine-tuning
training.dropout: 0.0 on JFT; 0.1 on ImageNet-21k and ImageNet; applied after every dense layer except qkv projections and directly after adding position to patch embeddings
training.regularisation: weight decay, dropout, label smoothing tuned on smaller datasets (label smoothing value not stated); gradient clipping at global norm 1 for ImageNet pre-training and for all fine-tuning; Polyak averaging factor 0.9999 for Table 2 ImageNet
training.compute: pre-training cost in TPUv3-core-days (Table 2): ViT-H/14 2.5k, ViT-L/16 JFT 0.68k, ViT-L/16 I21k 0.23k, BiT-L 9.9k, Noisy Student 12.3k; exaFLOPs per model in Table 6 (ViT-H/14 14 epochs 4262)
training.wall_clock: ViT-L/16 I21k: approximately 30 days on a standard cloud TPUv3 with 8 cores
training.seeds: mean and std over three fine-tuning runs (Table 2); pre-training seeds not stated

other.fine_tune_resolution: 384 by default; 512 for ViT-L/16 and 518 for ViT-H/14 for Table 2 ImageNet
other.position_embedding_resize: 2D interpolation of pre-trained position embeddings when resolution increases
other.few_shot_probe: regularized least-squares regression from frozen representation to {-1,1}^K targets, closed form
other.masked_patch_pretrain: corrupt 50% of patch embeddings (80% [mask] embedding, 10% random patch, 10% unchanged); Adam base LR 2e-4, warmup 10k, cosine decay, batch 4096, 1M steps (~14 epochs) on JFT; 15% corruption slightly worse
other.pretrain_table3_note: Table 3 lists R50x{1,2} 1e-3, R101x1 8e-4, R152x{1,2} 6e-4, R50+ViT-L/32 2e-4, hybrids otherwise as ViT counterparts

inference.samples: three fine-tuning runs per Table 2 cell

other.attention_maps: Attention Rollout (Abnar & Zuidema 2020) on ViT-L/16, averaged over heads, multiplied across layers

baselines: ResNet (BiT) family and hybrids in scaling study
eval.protocol: Fine-tune hyperparameters chosen by small grid search on held-out train sub-splits (10% Pets/Flowers, 2% CIFAR, 1% ImageNet), then retrain on full train and report test; mean +/- std of three fine-tuning runs in Table 2; early stopping with best validation accuracy in JFT subset study.

availability.data: JFT-300M is in-house and not released; ImageNet, ImageNet-21k, VTAB public

evidence.quote: All models are trained with a batch size of 4096 and learning rate warmup of 10k steps.

limits: Only image classification is evaluated; detection and segmentation are named as open challenges.
Best results depend on JFT-300M, an unreleased in-house dataset; on ImageNet alone ViT-L is below ViT-B and below same-size ResNets.
Compute-efficiency claims are caveated: the authors say pre-training efficiency may depend on schedule, optimizer and weight decay, not just architecture.
Self-supervised pre-training is preliminary and 4% behind supervised; contrastive pre-training left for future work.
Fine-tuning and linear few-shot used for different figures; the few-shot study of ViT is left as future work.
Label smoothing value, precision, hardware counts and pre-training seeds are not stated.
Axial attention variants are better in accuracy but cost more compute; AxialResNet implementation was too slow on TPUs for large-scale runs.
Dated: in 2026 ViT is the standard vision backbone; later work (not in this paper) showed it can train on ImageNet-only with stronger augmentation.

figures.caption: Model overview. We split an image into fixed-size patches, linearly embed each of them, add position embeddings, and feed the resulting sequence of vectors to a standard Transformer encoder.
